# Tersa language spec (compact, for LLMs)

Tersa is a statically typed language that compiles to Python 3.10+. Syntax is Python-like (indentation, `:` blocks, `#` comments) but stricter. Files end in `.tsa`. Run: `tersa run file.tsa`. Check only: `tersa check file.tsa --json`.

## Values and types
int float str bool | [T] list | {K: V} map | set[T] | (A, B) tuple | T? optional | T!E result | fn(A) -> R | dyn (unchecked, for JSON/Python interop) | () unit
Literals: 42 3.14 1_000 "text" r"raw {no interp}" """multi-line""" true false none [1, 2] {"a": 1} (1, "x")
Strings interpolate with braces: "hi {name}, {n + 1}", with Python format specs: "{price:.2f} {n:>5} {ratio:.1%}". Literal braces: {{ }}.

## Variables
x = 5            # immutable; declares x (type inferred)
var n = 0        # mutable
n += 1           # only var can be reassigned or mutated (push, x[i] = v, x.f = v)
y: float = 1     # optional annotation
a, b = pair      # unpack tuple or list
A name can be declared once per function. Variables are block-scoped.

## Functions
fn add(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    a + b                      # last expression is the return value
fn sq(x: float) = x * x        # return type may be omitted: it is inferred (still type-checked)
fn greet(name: str, loud: bool = false):     # infers no return value
    print(if loud: name.upper() else: name)
Recursive functions must declare their return type: fn fact(n: int) -> int = if n <= 1: 1 else: n * fact(n - 1)
fn grow(var xs: [int]) = xs.push(1)          # var param: function may mutate the argument
Call: add(1, 2), greet("a", loud=true). Method-call syntax works for any function: xs.len() == len(xs), add(1, 2) == 1.add(2).
Method syntax looks up, in order: the type's own methods, built-ins, then your functions whose first parameter fits.
Lambdas: x => x * 2, (a, b) => a + b, () => 0. Generics: fn first[T](xs: [T]) -> T? = xs.first()
Constraints: [N: num] (int/float), [T: ord] (comparable), [T: hash] (map key).

## Control flow
if x > 0: print("pos")
elif x < 0: print("neg")
else: print("zero")
label = if x > 0: "pos" else: "other"      # if is an expression (needs else)
for i in 0..10: ...        # 0..10 excludes 10, 0..=10 includes it
for i, item in xs.enumerate(): ...
for k, v in m.items(): ...
while cond: ...            # break, continue, pass
Conditions must be bool: no truthiness. Write len(xs) > 0, x != none, n != 0.

## Records and choice types
type Point(x: float, y: float = 0.0)          # record (immutable)
type Account(owner: str, var balance: int)     # var field can be changed
p = Point(1.0, y=2.0); p.x; p2 = p.with(x=5.0)
fn Point.norm() -> float = sqrt(self.x ** 2 + self.y ** 2)    # method; self is implicit
type Shape = Circle(r: float) | Rect(w: float, h: float) | Empty
type Tree[T] = Leaf | Node(left: Tree[T], val: T, right: Tree[T])
type Grid = [[int]]                            # alias

## match (must be exhaustive; the compiler lists missing cases)
fn area(s: Shape) -> float:
    match s:
        Circle(r): 3.14159 * r * r
        Rect(w, h): w * h
        Empty: 0.0
Patterns: literals, _ (anything), name (binds), Variant(a, b), (a, b), none, some(x), ok(v), err(e), 1 | 2 | 3. Guards: x if x > 0: ...

## Optionals: T? (none instead of null; the compiler forces you to handle it)
fn find(id: int) -> str?:
    if id == 1: return "alice"     # a T is automatically a T?
    none
n = find(2)
if n != none: print(n.upper())     # n is str inside this block
name = find(2) ?? "anon"           # default (?? binds tighter than + - * /)
v = find(1)!                       # unwrap; panics if none
Inside a fn returning U?, `x?` returns none early when x is none.

## Errors: T!E results (no exceptions)
fn parse_age(s: str) -> int!str:
    n = s.parse_int()                  # parse_int returns int?
    if n == none: return err("not a number: {s}")
    ok(n)
fn total(xs: [str]) -> int!str:
    var sum = 0
    for x in xs:
        sum += parse_age(x)?           # ? returns the error early
    ok(sum)
fn save(path: str, text: str) -> !str:  # !E means ()!E: an action that can fail
    if text == "": return err("empty")
    write_file(path, text)?            # falling off the end returns ok(())
match total(["1", "2"]):
    ok(v): print(v)
    err(e): print("failed: {e}")
r! unwraps or panics; r ?? 0 gives a default. Ignoring a Result is a compile error (use _ = r to ignore on purpose).
panic("msg") stops the program. assert cond, "msg".

## Built-in functions (all also callable as methods: s.upper())
print(a, b, ...) str(x) int(f) float(i) parse_int(s) -> int? parse_float(s) -> float? len(x) is_empty(x)
abs min max sum clamp round floor ceil sqrt sin cos tan log exp random() rand_int(lo, hi) choice shuffle pi inf
str: upper lower trim trim_start trim_end split(sep?) lines join(sep) replace(old, new) starts_with ends_with
     find(sub) -> int? count(sub) chars reverse pad_left(n, fill) pad_right is_digit is_alpha contains fmt(x, digits) ord chr
     s * 3 repeats; s[1:3] slices; "x" in s
list: push pop insert(i, x) remove_at(i) remove(x) extend clear  (these mutate: need var)
      map filter fold(init, (acc, x) => ...) any all count find(pred) -> T? index_of(x) -> int? first last get(i) -> T?
      sort sort_by(key) sort_desc reverse min_by max_by enumerate zip flatten unique group_by(key) copy
      (sort/map/filter/reverse return NEW lists; xs + ys concatenates; [x * 2 for x in xs if x > 0])
map:  m[k] (panics if missing) get(k) -> V? keys values items remove(k) merge(other) contains; k in m; m[k] = v (var)
set:  set(xs) set() add remove union intersect difference to_list; x in s
io:   input(prompt) args() read_file(path) -> str!str write_file(path, text) -> ()!str append_file file_exists env(name) -> str?
      now() sleep(sec) to_json(x) parse_json(s) -> dyn!str exit(code)
dyn values (from JSON or Python) allow any operation; convert with `as`: data["age"] as int (checked at runtime).

## Modules and Python interop
use geometry               # imports public names from geometry.tsa (path relative to the main file); names starting with _ are private
use geometry: area, Shape  # only these
use lib.geometry as g      # qualified: g.area(s)
extern "math":             # call any Python module with declared types
    fn gcd(a: int, b: int) -> int
    tau: float
extern "pathlib":
    type Path(name: str)            # opaque Python type with readable fields
    fn Path(p: str) -> Path as path # import under another name
    fn Path.exists() -> bool        # Python method

## Tests
test "adds":
    assert add(2, 3) == 5
Run with: tersa test file.tsa

## Common mistakes the compiler rejects (and how to fix)
str + int -> use "{x}" interpolation | if xs: -> if len(xs) > 0: | x.upper() when x is str? -> handle none first
reassigning a non-var -> declare with var | xs.sort() alone -> xs = xs.sort() | non-exhaustive match -> add arms
b = a then mutating b (a is a list/map) -> var b = a.copy()
int("5") -> parse_int("5") ?? 0 | null/None/nil -> none | && || ! -> and or not | 'single quotes' -> "double quotes"
